alt: Three cards compare the components of 0457: the Written Exam assesses research, analysis and evaluation; the Individual Report adds reflection and communication; the Team Project is where collaboration is assessed. Below, Component 2 facts: 30% of the qualification, 60 marks, 1500 to 2000 words, internally set and externally marked.
caption: The Individual Report is the most independent component and assesses five of the six skills.

alt: A narrowing funnel: a topic from the syllabus list, then its context, then a global issue with present-day impact that divides opinion, and finally a global research question that becomes the report title.
caption: Each step narrows the focus until one researchable question is left.

alt: A river runs from an upstream country to a downstream country. The upstream government prioritises its own agriculture; the downstream government faces shortages. The report compares both perspectives, then weighs actions such as a joint water-sharing treaty or an independent monitoring body.
caption: A good question sets up at least two perspectives that the report can compare.

alt: Four numbered steps: explain the issue and its perspectives; analyse causes and consequences; evaluate possible courses of action and justify one; reflect and conclude by answering the research question.
caption: Following the recommended sequence makes each requirement easy to evidence.

alt: A bar split into AO1 (40 marks), AO2 reflection (5 marks) and AO3 communication (15 marks). Underneath, the eight marking tables: global issue, causes and consequences, perspectives, courses of action, evaluation of sources, reflection, structure and clarity, and referencing.
caption: Two-thirds of the marks sit in the five AO1 tables.

alt: Side-by-side comparison. The title Climate change is too broad. A question such as To what extent should a named country restrict a named industry to protect a named resource names a place and an issue, allows more than one perspective and gives enough structure for the word count.
caption: Start with the question, not the topic.

alt: One source branches into two jobs. AO1 evaluation: explain its value and judge whether it is reliable and credible. AO3 communication: cite it with a complete, consistent, clearly linked referencing system.
caption: Evaluating a source and referencing it are marked separately.
